notes: Notes: Only the 23 stars with individual HVS/Gaia identifiers in Table 1 are identifiable. The 17 above-threshold observed stars are HVS01, HVS02, HVS03, HVS04, HVS05, HVS06, HVS07, HVS08, HVS09, HVS10, HVS11, HVS12, HVS13, HVS14, HVS15, HVS16, and HVS17; the other 132 of the 149 candidates (T:p3-b4, T:p8-b8) are not individually listed, and the 13 previously suggested HVSs among them are unnamed (T:p8-b10). HVS18, HVS19, HVS20, HVS21, HVS22, and HVS23 are omitted from candidates_found: T:p3-b9 calls them six control stars wrongly included in the preliminary follow-up list with P_esc,0 < 50%, T:p4-b0 places them below the P_esc,0 = 50% line, and their final P_esc values in T:p6-b0 are 49.2%, 43.3%, 38.2%, 38.7%, 19.5%, and 16.9%; T:p5-b9 describes such low-P_esc objects as HiVel stars. The abstract and T:p9-b4 say 23 of the 149 sources were analyzed, but this conflicts with the six controls; the 132 remaining (T:p8-b8, T:p9-b5) is consistent with 149 - 17 = 132. HVS01, HVS02, and HVS03 are follow_up because T:p3-b9 states they were previously proposed as HVSs (Du et al. 2019; Scholz 2024) and included for spectroscopy; HVS01 was excluded by Scholz 2024 and flagged as a CEMP candidate but retained (T:p3-b10). T:p5-b2 says the HVS candidates retain classification after FORS2, but T:p8-b3/Table 3 show only HVS01 and HVS02 (three with the bar) have P_esc >= 50% under McMillan (2017); I retain HVS04, HVS05, HVS06, HVS07, HVS08, HVS09, HVS10, HVS11, HVS12, HVS13, HVS14, HVS15, HVS16, and HVS17 as candidates_found because the paper continues to call them HVS candidates and Table 2 gives P_esc > 50% under MWPotential2014. HVS02 is also labeled 'Disk crossing / Extra-Galactic' in Table 2.

HVS01: No parallax, distance, or proper-motion measurements for HVS01 are reported in the supplied material. The r_min values in Table 2 (T:p6-b0) and Table 3 (T:p9-b0) are minimum past Galactocentric distances, not the present-day galactocentric radius, so they are not recorded as galactocentric_radius. P_esc is explicitly defined in Table 2 as the probability of being unbound from the Milky Way; a bound probability is not separately reported.

HVS02: Table 2 also reports z = 2.1 ± 0.4 kpc and past minimum Galactocentric distance r_min = 8.0 ± 0.3 kpc for HVS02; r_min is not the present-day galactocentric radius, so it was not recorded under galactocentric_radius. No individual parallax, distance, or proper-motion values for HVS02 are given in the supplied material.

HVS03: Only quantities explicitly reported for HVS03 / Gaia DR3 4294774301679435776 are included. The P_esc,0 value and the P_esc values under several potentials are retained as distinct unbound-probability results. The r_min entries in T:p9-b0 are minimum Galactocentric distances reached on past orbits, not present-day Galactocentric radii, so they are not recorded as galactocentric_radius under the present-day-state rule. No present-day galactocentric radius, heliocentric distance, parallax, or proper motions are reported for this target in the supplied material. No bound probability is directly reported; it was not calculated.

HVS04: The supplied material does not report HVS04's present-day distance, parallax, proper-motion components, or current Galactocentric radius. Table 2 and Table 3 give r_min (minimum past Galactocentric distance), which is not the present-day galactocentric radius, so it is not included. P_esc is reported as the probability of being unbound; bound probabilities are not reported, and no conversion was made. Table 3's column label "MM55" is described in its notes as the McMillan (2017)+bar (MM+bar) potential; the reported value is retained under that condition.

HVS05: For HVS05 (Gaia DR3 6496426077183248256), the supplied material lists no individual parallax, proper motions, heliocentric distance, present-day Galactocentric radius, or bound probability. The tabulated r_min values are historical minimum Galactocentric distances, not current galactocentric radii, so they were not recorded as galactocentric_radius (T:p6-b0, T:p9-b0). P_esc,0=80.4% (T:p4-b0) and the post-v_los P_esc=83.7% (T:p6-b0) are both retained; alternative-potential P_esc values from Table 3 are also retained (I:p9-b0).

HVS06: HVS06 is identified as Gaia DR3 5673818825000094336 in Table 1 (I:p4-b0; T:p4-b0). The paper's P_esc and P_esc,0 are explicitly probabilities of being unbound from the Milky Way, so no separate bound probability is recorded. The r_min values in Tables 2 and 3 are minimum past Galactocentric distances, not present-day galactocentric radii, so they were not recorded as galactocentric_radius. No distance, parallax, or proper-motion values for HVS06 are reported in the supplied material. Table 3 reports additional P_esc values under different adopted Galactic potentials.

HVS07: Target star: HVS07 (Gaia DR3 6389682292902592256). The supplied tables do not report individual distance, parallax, or proper-motion values for this star. Table 2 gives r_min = 1.4 ± 0.4 kpc and Table 3 gives potential-specific r_min values, but these are minimum past Galactocentric distances, not present-day galactocentric radii, so they are omitted. The text's v_T = 710 ± 70 km/s near r_min is a past orbital value, not the present-day speed, and is omitted.

HVS08: Table 1 is at T:p4-b0, Table 2 at T:p6-b0, and Table 3 at T:p9-b0. HVS08 is a golden (G) target. The P_esc values are unbound probabilities; P_esc,0 is the initial estimate without a measured v_los. The paper's r_min values are minimum past Galactocentric distances, not present-day galactocentric radii, so they were not extracted as galactocentric_radius. No distance, parallax, proper motions, or present-day galactocentric radius for HVS08 are reported in the supplied material.

HVS09: The paper reports r_min (minimum Galactocentric distance reached in the past) for HVS09, but not its present-day Galactocentric radius; r_min values were therefore not recorded under galactocentric_radius, which is restricted here to the present-day state. No bound-probability values are reported, so none were derived from the escape probabilities.

HVS10: HVS10 is identified by HVS10 and Gaia DR3 3555961002414624640 in T:p4-b0. The P_esc values are probabilities of being unbound from the Milky Way; the paper does not report corresponding bound probabilities. The r_min values in T:p9-b0 are minimum past Galactocentric distances, not present-day galactocentric radii, so they were not extracted as galactocentric_radius. No individual parallax, distance, or proper-motion values for HVS10 are listed in the supplied tables.

HVS11: Table 1 (T:p4-b0) identifies HVS11 as Gaia DR3 6407392126691609600. The paper does not report target-specific distance, parallax, or proper motions. It reports past minimum Galactocentric distances for HVS11 (r_min = 7.2 ± 0.3 kpc in T:p6-b0 and about 7.3 ± 0.1 kpc under the potentials in T:p9-b0), but these are orbital minima rather than present-day Galactocentric radii, so they were not recorded under galactocentric_radius. Only unbound probabilities P_esc are explicitly reported; bound probabilities are not tabulated.

HVS12: HVS12 is identified as Gaia DR3 6318336357766371072. The paper does not report an individual parallax, distance, proper-motion components, or present-day galactocentric radius for HVS12. The r_min values in Tables 2 and 3 are minimum past Galactocentric distances, not present-day galactocentric radii, so they are not recorded as galactocentric_radius (T:p6-b0; T:p9-b0). P_esc,0 in Table 1 is an initial escape probability before the FORS2 radial velocity; Table 2 P_esc and the Table 3 potential-dependent P_esc values are retained separately (T:p4-b0; T:p6-b0; T:p9-b0).

HVS13: Table 2 and Table 3 list r_min, the minimum past Galactocentric distance, not HVS13's present-day galactocentric radius, so those values were not recorded as galactocentric_radius (T:p6-b0, T:p9-b0).
